subject: Safeguard and multi‑SKU floor/ceiling — markup and procurement questions
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@greenridge.io>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Safeguard and multi‑SKU floor/ceiling — initial markup

Elena —

Thanks again for the time this week. Per our call we attached a proposed redline to the pricing exhibit that implements the floor/ceiling guardrail we discussed. High level:

- We constrained the floor/ceiling to apply per SKU family (not across unrelated SKUs) to avoid cross-subsidization.
- Added a temporary promotional carveout for months 1–3 (detailed in the annex).
- Built a quarterly true‑up bucket so overage credits flow back if the aggregate usage exceeds the ceiling unexpectedly.

Attachments: 20280427-GR-price-exhibit-redline.pdf (annotated), multi-sku-schedule.xlsx (mapping of SKU families).

Can you confirm whether procurement needs the floor/ceiling defined at the invoice line level or if the SKU family definition is sufficient for your billing system? If invoice-line required we may need to adjust the order form wording and push a small amendment.

If helpful, Marissa and I can hop on a 20‑minute call this afternoon to walk through the change.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0148
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morris <elena@greenridge.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@greenridge.io
Date: 2028-04-27T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Safeguard and multi‑SKU floor/ceiling — initial markup

Jordan —

Appreciate the redline, and the SKU family approach looks promising. A few procurement items before we escalate to legal:

1) Our invoicing platform requires the billing guardrail to map to invoice line items (we bill by product_code). Can the SKU family be surfaced as an invoice line attribute so finance can reconcile automatically?

2) The promotional carveout is acceptable but procurement needs a hard end-date and an obligation to notify if Redwood intends to extend it. Please add a 15‑day notice clause.

3) Regarding the quarterly true‑up: will credits be issued as a refund or as a future invoice credit? We prefer invoice credits.

Attaching a short procurement checklist (procure@greenridge.io). If you can update the order form to call out product_code-level mapping and the 15‑day notice, we can move to legal review this afternoon.

Thanks —
Elena Morris
Director, Vendor Ops
GreenRidge Analytics
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com 
To: Elena Morris <elena@greenridge.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-27T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Safeguard and multi‑SKU floor/ceiling — procurement points and legal rationale

Elena / Jordan —

Thanks for the close review. A couple of notes from legal on the requested changes:

- Invoice line mapping: we can add explicit language that the floor/ceiling will be applied at the product_code level as reflected in the attached multi-sku-schedule.xlsx. That will satisfy finance while preserving the guardrail semantics.

- Promotional carveout: we will add a 15‑day written notice requirement for any extension and a maximum extension window (one additional 3‑month period) to prevent open-ended promotions.

- Credit handling: Redwood prefers to issue invoice credits (applied to the next invoice) rather than refunds for operational simplicity — we'll confirm the mechanics in the order form.

Redlines: I'm attaching a Word copy with tracked changes (20280427-orderform-redline.docx) to make it easy for your counsel to import. If GreenRidge legal wants to suggest alternative wording, please flag exact line numbers.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Elena Morris <elena@greenridge.io>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@greenridge.io
Date: 2028-04-27T12:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Safeguard and multi‑SKU floor/ceiling — procurement points and legal rationale

Laura —

That approach works in principle. A couple of clarifying asks from GreenRidge legal:

- Can Redwood confirm that the product_code mapping in the spreadsheet is non-exhaustive and that any future product_codes will default to the same SKU family unless otherwise specified? We want to avoid having to reopen redlines when new products ship.

- For invoice credits: request that credits be automatically applied within 30 days of the true‑up calculation. Is that acceptable?

If yes to both, we will have counsel incorporate and return redlines by EOD. Otherwise we'll propose alternative language.

Elena
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@greenridge.io>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-27T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Safeguard and multi‑SKU floor/ceiling — scheduling quick sync

Elena —

Happy to confirm:

- Product_code defaulting: yes — we will include a clause that new product_codes inherit the SKU family mapping unless either party provides written notice within 30 days of launch. That should limit churn.

- Invoice credit timing: 30 days from true‑up is acceptable. We'll add explicit language showing the calculation timeline and the credit application window.

We can do a 20‑minute call at 4pm PT to run through the final tracked changes and get verbal agreement before your counsel turns around the final markup. Call invite sent.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Elena Morris <elena@greenridge.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-27T17:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Safeguard and multi‑SKU floor/ceiling — scheduling quick sync

Marissa / team —

4pm PT call worked well. GreenRidge legal will post the final two line edits (product_code defaulting language and 30‑day credit window) into the Word doc and return by 6pm PT. Once we have that, we can route for signature.

Please confirm whether Redwood prefers DocuSign or a countersigned PDF for execution — procurement prefers DocuSign.

Thanks everyone — moving fast on this which is great.

Elena
Procurement, GreenRidge Analytics
